treatment: Remove severely infected leaves where practical and apply a locally approved triazole or strobilurin fungicide according to label guidance.
prevention: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, improve field drainage, and scout after humid or rainy periods.

treatment: Correct nutrient deficiencies and use a registered fungicide if lesions are widespread.
prevention: Use clean seed, balanced fertilization, and avoid drought stress.

treatment: Use threshold-based control with recommended biological or selective insecticide treatment targeted into the whorl.
prevention: Scout weekly during vegetative growth, conserve natural enemies, and remove volunteer host plants.

treatment: Remove infected material and apply a registered protectant or systemic fungicide according to local guidance.
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation, increase spacing, remove crop debris, and monitor closely in cool wet weather.

treatment: Remove infected lower leaves and apply a registered fungicide when lesions spread beyond the lower canopy.
prevention: Rotate crops, mulch soil, improve airflow, and avoid wetting foliage during irrigation.

treatment: Use copper-based sprays where approved and remove heavily infected plants to reduce spread.
prevention: Use certified seed, avoid working wet plants, and rotate with non-host crops.

treatment: Improve ventilation and apply a registered fungicide if mold is spreading on upper leaves.
prevention: Reduce humidity, increase spacing, prune lower leaves, and scout protected crops weekly.

treatment: Remove infected lower leaves and apply protectant fungicide when spotting moves up the plant.
prevention: Mulch, stake plants, rotate fields, and destroy old crop residue.

treatment: Use threshold-based acaricide or approved biological control when mite colonies are visible on many leaves.
prevention: Avoid drought stress, reduce dust, conserve predators, and scout during hot dry periods.

treatment: Improve airflow and apply a registered fungicide if lesions spread to new leaves and fruit.
prevention: Rotate crops, remove debris, avoid overhead irrigation, and maintain plant spacing.

treatment: Remove infected plants early and control whitefly vectors using approved methods.
prevention: Use virus-free seedlings, install reflective mulches where practical, and monitor whitefly populations.

treatment: Remove infected plants and disinfect tools; there is no cure once plants are infected.
prevention: Use resistant varieties, certified seed, and sanitize hands and tools between plants.

treatment: Apply registered fungicide when lesions appear on middle canopy leaves and continue on a protective schedule.
prevention: Rotate crops, maintain balanced nutrition, and remove infected debris after harvest.

treatment: Destroy infected tubers and foliage where practical and apply blight fungicide immediately when active.
prevention: Use certified seed, scout after rain, improve drainage, and destroy volunteer potatoes.

treatment: Remove heavily infected leaves and apply a registered fungicide if lesions spread across the bed.
prevention: Use resistant cultivars where available, avoid overhead irrigation, and maintain bed sanitation.

treatment: Apply a registered rust fungicide when active pustules appear on upper leaves and disease is spreading.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties, destroy volunteer wheat, and monitor after humid weather.

treatment: Confirm with field history or soil testing and apply nitrogen using local crop recommendations.
prevention: Use soil tests, split fertilizer applications, and maintain organic matter.
